about: Shot list for the < 2:00 demo video (SPEC 10). capture.mjs records every shot whose status is 'ready' or 'stand-in'; see video/README.md. Each shot loads its URL fresh, runs 'setup' off camera, then records 'actions'. 'hold' is screen time in seconds after an action; waits use selectors, never sleeps. VO: no digits or number words; a number comes in only as a {claim.value} slot, filled from the verified claims the page shows, else 'vo_fallback' is used.

shots.title: Before kick-off: the fictional line-ups and their scanning habits
shots.vo: Before kick-off: every player, and every look over his shoulder in this move.

shots.title: Cold open in first person: the look over the shoulder, a runner appears
shots.notes: Free play at 0.5x from just before the key scan; the app slows further around the scan. Crop to the first-person view (manifest.json gives the box).

shots.title: Broadcast camera with live overlays (sprint tag, pass speed); the move plays out
shots.pending: Broadcast camera (SPEC 7) is not on main. Stand-in: the live stream in the current split view, with the sprint tag in the header and the moment card when it is detected.
shots.vo: A synthetic match with fictional clubs, streamed live from our API on Azure. As it plays, the system flags the moments worth explaining.
shots.notes: Re-record when the broadcast camera lands: add its toggle to the actions and change status to ready.

shots.title: Breakdown: freeze, POV through the scans, the key scan lights up the runner, freeze at the pass
shots.vo: Our agent crew builds the replay. Back inside his head: the scans before the ball arrived, and the key look that showed him the runner. When he played the pass, his picture of the runner was off by {belief_error.err} metres.
shots.vo_fallback: Our agent crew builds the replay. Back inside his head: the scans before the ball arrived, and the key look that showed him the runner.
shots.notes: The plan's length is the Telestrator's; trim in the edit. Captions are the app's verified lines.

shots.title: Toggle With / Without the look: without it he passes back (counterfactual ghost)
shots.vo: Now take that look away and re-run the simulation. Without it, he plays it safe and passes back. That look was worth {cf_value.dxt} in expected threat.
shots.vo_fallback: Now take that look away and re-run the simulation. Without it, he plays it safe and passes back.
shots.notes: The highlight of the video. Frozen at the decision, the pass options flip between the runs; then the run without the look plays on with the other run's ghost path.

shots.title: The same moment for casual / analyst / player-fan
shots.vo: The same moment, told for a casual fan, an analyst or a fan of the player.
shots.notes: A breakdown not yet cached takes about ten seconds to generate: cut the wait (manifest.json has each action's time).

shots.title: en <-> zh
shots.notes: The captions over the first-person view switch to Chinese.

shots.title: Open one caption's evidence
shots.vo: Every line opens its evidence: each claim, its kind, its verdict, and the frame that proves it.
shots.notes: Clicking the caption pauses the breakdown, opens the evidence card under the views and seeks to the evidence frame.

shots.title: Ask a what-if: suggested question, then a free question to the live service

actions.name: What if he passed to H4?

actions.label: Ask your own question
actions.text: What if he had carried it forward?

actions.question: What if he had carried it forward?

shots.vo: Ask what if. The simulator forces that choice and replays the moment, and the answer is verified like everything else.
shots.notes: Scrolled 160 px so the tactical board (ghost path) and the answer are both in frame. Suggested answers are precomputed and verified; the free question goes to the live service. The app's own example (back to the centre-back) is refused by the rule matcher when the model is capped, so the shot asks one that maps to an option either way.

shots.title: The verifier blocks a wrong number and a banned judgement word
shots.pending: No view on main shows the verifier blocking a line (the narration panel only lists withheld lines). Not captured until such a view exists.
shots.vo: Before anything airs, the verifier checks every number against the simulation. A wrong number is blocked, and so is a judgement like 'he should have'.
shots.notes: Candidates once built: a producer-console view of a rejected draft with its verdict and the banned-word hit.
